gaps: ONERROR GOLABEL /Error — PML1 error-trap syntax; KB only documents handle/elsehandle/endhandle blocks, not ONERROR/GOLABEL.
LABEL /Error — PML1 label definition; KB has 'goto' keyword but no explicit LABEL definition example.
SAVEWORK — PML1 command for saving work; not listed in KB syntax reference.
UNCLAIM ALL — PML1 command for releasing claims; not listed in KB syntax reference.
inset — PML1 set-membership operator (e.g. |VOID| inset array); KB operator table covers LT/GT/NE/LE/GE but not inset.
matchwild — PML1 wildcard match function; not in KB operator/function table.
ONERROR → GOLABEL → LABEL → handle block → FINISH error recovery pattern — KB has isolated handle blocks but not the ONERROR/GOLABEL macro-level error-trap pattern.

COLLECT ALL ... with ($!dynamicFilter) — nested dynamic COLLECT ALL inside a DO loop with variable substitution in the filter string; KB has COLLECT ALL examples but not with $! variable substitution inside the expression.
2D ARRAY initialization via !arr[i][j] = value — KB has ARRAY methods (Append, Size) but no 2D initialization example.
Macro-level structure: ONERROR at top → imports/using → global logger init → data setup → COLLECT ALL iteration → error LABEL with handle → FINISH. This top-level flow is not exemplified in KB.
Error handler re-uses DATETIME() for timestamping — the pattern of re-initialising datetime inside an error handler block is not documented.
!!global prefix used for logger object (!!ramCommonLogger) and external function (!!jacExportRDLDataReportMatrix); KB mentions !!global convention but does not show macro-level usage.
Customer-specific naming: RAMCOMMONLOGGER, jacExportRDLDataReportMatrix, writeErrorDataToExcel — these are project-specific and not in KB (expected).
Empty-pattern detection: split string into array, then append additional empty-value patterns (| |, ||, 0ampere) — KB has split() but not this sentinel-detection pattern.
Replacement sentinel map: array of 'value;NA' pairs for filtering invalid readings — this business-logic pattern is not in KB.
Nested COLLECT ALL: inner query uses $!tagFilter with variable substitution — boundary condition when inner query returns 0 elements (guarded by size gt 0 check).
import 'GridControl' — PML add-in import; KB mentions add-ins but has no import example for GridControl.
import 'Aveva.Engineering.Tags.Pml' — AVEVA module import; KB has using namespace examples but not import of AVEVA module objects.
External objects: RAMCOMMONLOGGER (custom logger), jacExportRDLDataReportMatrix (custom export function), writeErrorDataToExcel — none are in KB.
Custom types: :RAMCommissioningPackage, ENGITE — PDMS element types specific to project.

newEntriesNeeded.title: ONERROR / GOLABEL / LABEL error trap in PML macros
newEntriesNeeded.principle: PML1 macros use ONERROR to redirect control to a named LABEL; the LABEL is paired with a handle block for cleanup.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Place ONERROR GOLABEL /LabelName at the top of the macro. Define LABEL /LabelName near FINISH. Inside the label, use handle any to capture the error context and perform cleanup (SAVEWORK, UNCLAIM ALL, logging).
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
ONERROR GOLABEL /LabelName
...
LABEL /LabelName
handle any
  -- cleanup
endhandle
FINISH
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_18_benchmark.pmlmac
ONERROR GOLABEL /Error
import 'GridControl'
handle any
endhandle
...
do !item values !list
  -- work
enddo
LABEL /Error
handle any
  SAVEWORK
  UNCLAIM ALL
  !!logger.writeError(...)
endhandle
FINISH
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- ❌ Missing ONERROR — errors crash the macro
import 'GridControl'
do !item values !list
  -- no error handling
enddo
FINISH
pitfalls: ONERROR must be placed before any import or using statements.
LABEL name must match exactly (case-insensitive but spelling must match).
FINISH must come after the error handler label block.

newEntriesNeeded.title: SAVEWORK and UNCLAIM ALL PDMS commands in PML macros
newEntriesNeeded.principle: SAVEWORK saves current database state; UNCLAIM ALL releases all element claims. Used in error recovery to prevent database lock.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Call SAVEWORK before UNCLAIM ALL in error handlers. UNCLAIM ALL should be called to release any element claims that may have been acquired during processing.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_18_benchmark.pmlmac
LABEL /Error
handle any
  SAVEWORK
  UNCLAIM ALL
  !!ramCommonLogger.writeErrorDataToExcel(...)
endhandle
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- ❌ UNCLAIM ALL without SAVEWORK — data loss risk
LABEL /Error
handle any
  UNCLAIM ALL
  -- SAVEWORK missing: unsaved changes lost
endhandle
pitfalls: SAVEWORK is slow on large databases — consider conditional save.
UNCLAIM ALL releases ALL claims; use UNCLAIM !ref for selective release.

newEntriesNeeded.title: PML1 inset and matchwild operators in query expressions
newEntriesNeeded.principle: PML1 provides set-membership (inset) and wildcard matching (matchwild) operators for query expressions in COLLECT ALL and other query commands.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use inset for membership testing: VALUE inset (|A|, |B|). Use matchwild for wildcard string matching: matchwild(string, pattern).
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_18_benchmark.pmlmac
!tagFilter = 'NOT(:TagStatus inset (|VOID|, |Future|)) and ISNAMED'
!tagFilter = !tagFilter & 'matchwild(namn of :TagRefToMCPackage, |*$!<commPckg.namn>*|)'
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- ❌ Using 'in' instead of 'inset'
!result = !value in (|A|, |B|)  -- not valid PML
pitfalls: inset expects a parenthesised list of values, not an array.
matchwild pattern uses * for any characters and ? for single character.
matchwild is a function call, not an operator — use matchwild(string, pattern).

newEntriesNeeded.title: 2D array initialization in PML
newEntriesNeeded.principle: PML arrays can be indexed with multiple subscripts: array[i][j] for 2D data. Initialize by assigning individual cells.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Create the array with ARRAY(), then assign cells using !arr[i][j] = value. There is no native 2D array literal — each cell must be assigned individually.
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_18_benchmark.pmlmac
!commonAttributes = object ARRAY()
!commonAttributes[1][1] = ':RAMTagOwner'
!commonAttributes[1][2] = 'Tag Owner'
!commonAttributes[2][1] = ':TagStatus'
!commonAttributes[2][2] = 'Tag Status'
pitfalls: PML ARRAY does not support multi-dimensional literals — each cell must be assigned.
Appending to a 2D array requires careful management of the outer array size.

newEntriesNeeded.title: COLLECT ALL with $! variable substitution in filter expressions
newEntriesNeeded.principle: PML allows $! variable substitution inside COLLECT ALL filter strings, enabling dynamic queries inside loops.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Use $!varName inside the COLLECT ALL with () expression to substitute the current loop variable's value into the filter string.
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
do !item values !list
  !filter = 'attribute eq |$!<item.attr>*|'
  var !results collect all (TYPE) with ($!filter)
  -- process results
enddo
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_18_benchmark.pmlmac
do !commPckgName values !commPckgList
  !commPckg = !commPckgName.dbref()
  !tagFilter = 'NOT(:TagStatus inset (|VOID|, |Future|)) and ISNAMED and matchwild(namn of :TagRefToMCPackage, |*$!<commPckg.namn>*|)'
  var !tagList collect all (ENGITE) with ($!tagFilter)
enddo
pitfalls: $! substitution only works inside pipe-delimited strings within COLLECT ALL expressions.
Variable must be a simple reference — method chains like $!<item.method()> are not supported.
Ensure the loop variable is resolved before the COLLECT ALL executes.

newEntriesNeeded.title: FINISH keyword in PML macros
newEntriesNeeded.principle: FINISH terminates macro execution cleanly. It should be placed at the end of the macro, after any error handler LABEL.
newEntriesNeeded.rule: Place FINISH as the last statement in the macro, after the error handler LABEL block. FINISH ensures clean exit and resource release.
newEntriesNeeded.syntax:
LABEL /Error
handle any
  -- error cleanup
endhandle
FINISH
newEntriesNeeded.exampleCanonical:
-- CB mac_18_benchmark.pmlmac
LABEL /Error
handle any
  SAVEWORK
  UNCLAIM ALL
  !!ramCommonLogger.writeErrorDataToExcel(...)
endhandle
FINISH
newEntriesNeeded.exampleAntipattern:
-- ❌ Code after FINISH (never executes)
FINISH
-- This line is unreachable
pitfalls: FINISH after LABEL means the label block is only reachable via ONERROR GOLABEL, not via normal flow.
If FINISH is placed before the error handler, the error handler is dead code.
